attributes: Hermaphrodite has exactly 302 neurons (male 385) with ~7,000 chemical synapses plus gap junctions — every neuron named, positioned and wired in published connectomes. Learning is synaptic plasticity inside a fully enumerated circuit — which is why this record can be scientist-grade.

attributes: When injured, sick or old, the medusa can collapse to a cyst-like stage and revert to a polyp — restarting its life cycle via transdifferentiation of its own cells. Nervous system is a cnidarian nerve net with a nerve ring — no brain.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — life-cycle reversion is documented in laboratory culture; any 'cognition' beyond nerve-net responses is inference, and there is very little to infer: this is a record about persistence, not intelligence.
brain_profile.architecture: Nerve net plus marginal nerve ring coordinating bell pulsation and tentacle responses. No centralisation, no learning studies of note. The remarkable system here is cellular, not neural: differentiated cells reprogram themselves back to a juvenile colony form.

cognition_model.summary: Not a thinker — a restarter. Its fame is a cellular trick: when the medusa fails, it does not only die; it can fold back into its own polyp stage and begin again. The Atlas records the trick precisely, without the magic the nickname implies.

skills: Colonial polyp growth and medusa budding

Both halves are in this record.
brain_profile.architecture: Planarian plan: bilobed brain integrating eyespot light, chemoreception and tactile input; ventral cords run the body. Learning paradigms show habituation, classical conditioning and maze performance. The radical datum is persistence: memories trained before decapitation were reported retained after a new brain regenerated — implying memory storage distributed or re-imprinted outside the original brain tissue.

origin: Real species; a plasmodial slime mould — a single giant multinucleate cell that creeps as a yellow network over rotting wood worldwide. No neurons, no brain, no cells-within-cells in its feeding stage. REAL shelf.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)

attributes: The plasmodium is one enormous cell with millions of nuclei, streaming cytoplasm through vein-like tubes whose thickness adapts to flow. It solves mazes by pruning to the shortest oat-to-oat path, builds networks comparable in efficiency to rail systems in famous experiments, habituates to harmless repellents (caffeine/quinine bridges, 2016), and anticipates periodic events after training in published work.

brain_profile.grade_note: MEASURED — habituation, maze-solving and network optimisation are published experimental results; 'learning' here means documented behavioural change from experience in an aneural system, and the record uses exactly that definition.
brain_profile.architecture: No nervous system whatsoever. Cognition, if the word is used, is hydrodynamics plus chemistry: tube conductance adapts to flux (more flow, thicker tube), repellent and attractant gradients bias growth, and cytoplasmic oscillation patterns encode timing. Memory lives in tube morphology and in deposited slime trails — the network outside the 'mind' remembers where the mind has been (it avoids its own slime: externalised spatial memory).

origin: Real species; carnivorous plant native only to a small wetland region around Wilmington, North Carolina. No neurons, no muscles — a counting plant. REAL shelf.

attributes: Each trap is a modified leaf: two lobes with trigger hairs, which snap shut in ~100 ms when triggered. The counting mechanism is published: one touch raises a signal but does not close the trap; a second touch within roughly 20-30 seconds crosses the threshold, fires action potentials, and closes it. Further struggles by prey trigger digestive-enzyme production scaled to touch counts — the plant counts to two to close, and higher to invest in digestion.

brain_profile.grade_note: MEASURED — the two-touch counting window and the touch-scaled enzyme response are published experimental results (Böhm et al. 2016 and successors).
brain_profile.architecture: No nervous system: electrical action potentials (plant-style, calcium-based) propagate through the leaf, and a short-lived chemical/electrical trace of the first touch is the 'memory' the second touch reads. Snap closure is turgor mechanics — stored elastic energy released by cell changes. A memory of seconds, implemented in ions.

regions.role: Touch detection on the trap surface

regions.role: Two touches within ~20-30 s = closure; more touches = digestion investment

attributes: Large, furry social bee with a brain of roughly a million-plus neurons (order-of-magnitude hymenopteran scale; species estimates vary). Workers learn flower colours/odours rapidly, copy techniques from demonstrators — pulling strings and rolling balls to reach reward in experiments, with the behaviour spreading through the colony socially (2016-2017, published in Science / PLOS Biology). Colonies are annual, founded by a single queen, a few hundred workers at peak.

brain_profile.grade_note: MEASURED — the string-pulling and ball-rolling social-learning results, plus flower-learning and trade-off studies, are published experimental findings on this species.
brain_profile.architecture: Hymenopteran plan like the pilot honeybee — mushroom bodies for associative learning, optic lobes, antennal lobes — in a larger, hardier bee. Social learning is the headline: an observer bee acquires a novel technique by watching a trained demonstrator, a capacity once assumed beyond insects.

attributes: Armoured body with ten eyes, including lateral compound eyes whose sensitivity is boosted up to a million-fold at night by a circadian clock in the brain — among the largest known day/night sensitivity swings. Males find females visually at the shore in spawning season. Blood (blue, copper-based) clots via amebocytes — the basis of the LAL endotoxin test used worldwide in medicine.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — visual physiology is MEASURED and Nobel-grade; whole-animal cognition beyond vision-guided behaviour is little studied, so the profile grades INFERRED.
brain_profile.architecture: Circumesophageal brain plus ventral cord. The famous system is retinal: lateral inhibition between ommatidia sharpens contrast (the Hartline-Ratliff equations), and efferent optic-nerve fibres from the brain retune the eye nightly — a brain that reaches out and recalibrates its own sensor on a clock.

cognition_model.summary: An eye with an animal attached, in the best sense: its retina taught science how neurons sharpen images, and its brain turns its own eyes up at night like a dial. Behaviour is seasonal and shore-bound — spawn at high spring tides, by sight and touch.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.

State changes: the eye's day/night modes are the clearest state change — a sensory animal with two visual physiologies.
relationships: Class Merostomata, order Xiphosura — a chelicerate, kin to spiders/scorpions, NOT a crustacean (the name lies; the record corrects it). Portia in this batch is its distant chelicerate cousin.

confidence_and_conflicts: The 'million-fold' sensitivity figure is the widely cited Barlow-lab result for circadian modulation — order-of-magnitude, condition-dependent. Learning/memory: an honest blank. MBTI is a behaviour-style metaphor over a mostly visual animal.
game_implementation: BrainKit: sensor-with-feedback agent — the brain modulates its own perception gain on a clock; spawning behaviour locked to tide/lunar timers.

attributes: A spiny sphere run by a nerve ring around the mouth plus five radial nerves — no brain, no head, no eyes (light sensitivity is dermal and via tube feet). Hundreds of tube feet taste and grip; the Aristotle's-lantern jaw apparatus grazes kelp and rock. Urchins aggregate, move toward food odours, cover themselves with shells/algae, and can strip kelp forests into 'urchin barrens' when predators (otters) vanish.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — anatomy and behaviour documented; with no central brain, 'cognition' is distributed sensorimotor economics, and the record frames it exactly that way.
brain_profile.architecture: Pentraradial nervous system: circumoral ring + radial cords; each arm-sector semi-autonomous, spines and tube feet locally reactive, whole-animal coordination by through-conduction. Chemosensation in tube feet steers slow migrations toward kelp; light and gravity orient covering behaviour.

relationships: Phylum Echinodermata — kin to Asterias in this batch (same phylum, same no-brain radial design; the Atlas pairs them). Ecological counterweight: sea otters keep it from eating the forest — a relationship, not a cognition.
memory_model: Remembers: no storage mechanism claimed. Habituation-like waning of responses is plausible in radial systems but is NOT claimed here without species evidence. Misreads: drift-kelp abundance can hold it in poor habitat — gradient-following has no foresight.
confidence_and_conflicts: An MBTI read on a brainless echinoderm is a design metaphor, labelled as such. Predator-response details vary across urchin species; this record stays with genus/family-documented behaviour and flags generalisations.

attributes: Five arms around a central disc, run by a circumoral nerve ring and a radial nerve per arm — no brain, no head. Each arm has an eyespot at its tip and semi-autonomous control of hundreds of tube feet. It prises mussels open with sustained tube-foot pull, everts its cardiac stomach into the shell, and digests prey externally. Lost arms regenerate; a detached arm with disc tissue can regrow a whole animal.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — anatomy, feeding and regeneration documented; arm-level autonomy is documented across asteroids and applied here at family level with the basis stated.
brain_profile.architecture: Radial plan like its urchin kin, but predatory: arms sample chemistry independently (tube feet), the ring integrates weakly, and a dominant arm often 'leads' locomotion toward prey odour. Behaviour is a negotiation among five sensory arms — direction emerges, it is not decreed.

attributes: Fast runner with cerci (rear sensors) that detect air puffs and trigger the famous giant-interneuron escape run in milliseconds — wind means predator, run first. Cockroaches learn mazes, places and odour associations in published experiments, groom fastidiously, aggregate by faecal pheromones, and thrive on almost any organic food. Despite folklore, it is not uniquely radiation-proof — hardier than humans, less so than some insects.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — escape circuitry is MEASURED-grade neurobiology; learning is documented across cockroach species with Periplaneta prominent historically, assembled here as INFERRED for the whole profile.
brain_profile.architecture: Insect plan pushed toward speed of escape: cercal afferents -> giant interneurons -> thoracic motor centres, bypassing deliberation. Above that reflex floor, a standard insect brain (mushroom bodies) supports place and odour learning — two gears: instant flight, and slow familiarity with a kitchen's map.

cognition_model.summary: A two-gear survivor: a hardwired hair-trigger escape for the next 50 milliseconds, and a learning brain that maps safe harbourages and food routes across weeks. Its genius is not invincibility — it is reflexes plus familiarity.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A pragmatic escape artist: exquisitely alert to threat, otherwise an unbothered opportunist that learns the building better than its owners know it.

skills: Giant-fibre escape response to air displacement
Maze and place learning (published cockroach studies)
Aggregation pheromone use and harborage fidelity
behavior_model: Triggers: air puff/shadow -> escape run to cover; darkness + pheromone-marked harborage -> aggregation. Needs: warmth, water, food scraps, crevices. Goals: feed at night, stay uncrushed, breed steadily. State changes: gravid females carry the ootheca and shift to protected sites; starved roaches range further and risk more.
relationships: Order Blattodea — which makes it, wonderfully, the termites' cousin (Macrotermes in this batch is a social cockroach lineage): solitary scavenger vs colony civilisation from one order.
memory_model: Remembers: harborage locations, food routes and trained cues for days-weeks in experiments. Forgets: unrewarded cues fade. Misreads: its escape trigger is deliberately over-inclusive — brooms, breezes and predators all mean run; false alarms are cheap, hesitation is not.
confidence_and_conflicts: Radiation-hardiness folklore is corrected, not repeated. Species attribution: escape-circuit classics are heavily Periplaneta; some learning paradigms used other roaches — family-level support, species-level caution, hence INFERRED.
game_implementation: BrainKit: dual-gear agent — hardwired reflex layer (fixed latency, no learning) under a mushroom-body familiarity map; fearfulness near-maximal on the reflex channel only.

attributes: A singing cricket (males chirp by stridulation) with a mushroom-body learning system dissected in unusual pharmacological detail: in Gryllus, octopamine mediates appetitive (reward) learning and dopamine aversive (punishment) learning in published experiments — in some respects the reverse emphasis of the fly. Crickets form long-term olfactory memories lasting days, and exhibit social song behaviour and aggressive male contests with winner-loser effects.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — the neuromodulator findings and conditioning are published (strong anchors); the whole-animal profile is assembled as INFERRED beside Drosophila's MEASURED connectome grade.
brain_profile.architecture: Orthopteran insect brain: antennal lobes -> mushroom bodies, with neuromodulator teaching signals whose identities are experimentally pinned in this genus. Auditory circuitry for song (own and rivals') runs in the thoracic ganglia, and aggression state is hormonally tuned (octopamine again — the cricket's arousal currency).

relationships: Order Orthoptera. Atlas relations: the neuromodulator mirror to Drosophila (reward chemistry weighted differently) — a comparison the Atlas map should make visible between the two insect learning records.
memory_model: Remembers: conditioned odours for days (long-term memory after adequate training); contest outcomes for hours. Forgets: single weak pairings decay. Misreads: winner effects can over-inflate aggression against stronger rivals — state, not assessment.
confidence_and_conflicts: Neuromodulator role assignments (octopamine=appetitive, dopamine=aversive) are the Mizunami group's Gryllus findings; they differ in emphasis from Drosophila, and the difference is real literature, not an error to harmonise. Species-level song/aggression detail draws partly on Gryllus generally.

attributes: Up to ~90 suckerless tentacles, pinhole eyes without lenses (camera obscura vision), and a brain markedly simpler than coleoid cephalopods — no dedicated vertical-lobe learning centre of the octopus/cuttlefish kind. Yet Crook & Basil (2008) showed it learns a light-food association with short- and long-term memory phases resembling coleoids', despite the missing hardware. It migrates vertically hundreds of metres daily and scavenges by smell.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — the 2008 learning/memory result is published; one study does not make a connectome, so the grade sits below Sepia's MEASURED, honestly.
brain_profile.architecture: Nautiloid plan: circumesophageal brain with fewer, larger lobes; olfaction dominant (rhinophores), vision coarse (pinhole). The scientific punch of the record: biphasic memory without the coleoid vertical lobe implies learning circuitry evolved differently — or more ancestrally — than the octopus design suggests.

State changes: day-deep / night-shallow vertical commuting is its master rhythm.

memory_model: Remembers: trained light-food association with short-term (hours) and longer phases in the 2008 paradigm. Forgets: untrained responses extinguish. Misreads: little studied — the record leaves the cell honestly empty rather than inventing errors.
confidence_and_conflicts: Single-study basis for the memory claim (Crook & Basil 2008) — published and peer-reviewed, but replication is thin; graded INFERRED for exactly that reason. Lifespan/depth figures are literature ranges.

attributes: Two epithelial layers with fibre cells between, ciliated below for gliding, a few millimetres across. It feeds by settling on algae and digesting externally beneath its body. Cells coordinate via peptide signals — it possesses much of the molecular toolkit that other animals built nervous systems from, deployed without a single neuron. Behaviour includes directed gliding, pausing on food, and body-shape changes coordinated across the disc.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — cell biology and behaviour documented; there is no cognition, and this record is the Atlas's proof that coordination predates neurons.
brain_profile.architecture: No nervous system, no synapses — but peptidergic secretory cells act as a slow broadcast network, the evolutionary raw material of neural signalling. Gliding coordination emerges from ciliary beating coupled through the epithelium: a consensus of cells with no conductor, simpler even than the sponge's arrangement in cell-type terms (though the sponge record holds the size record).

origin: Real species; soil social amoeba — free-living single cells that, when starved, aggregate by the hundred-thousand into a migrating slug and then a fruiting body, ~20% of cells dying to build the stalk. REAL shelf.

attributes: Amoebae hunt bacteria alone until food runs out; then cells pulse cAMP, neighbours relay the signal, and streams converge into a multicellular slug that migrates toward light and heat gradients, chooses where to fruit, and sacrifices its stalk cells so spores can disperse. Chimeras can cheat (under-contribute to stalk) — documented social conflict in a microbe. Some clones 'farm' bacteria, carrying food stocks into the fruiting body (published 2011).

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — aggregation signalling and slug behaviour are MEASURED-grade cell biology; framing the slug as a cognitive agent is the Atlas's colony-style modelling choice, stated openly (as with the termite colony record).
brain_profile.architecture: No neurons at any stage. Coordination is a relay: cAMP pulses propagate cell-to-cell, each cell both receiver and repeater — a chemical internet. The slug integrates light/heat/ammonia gradients across thousands of cells and 'decides' migration vs fruiting as a population-level computation.

origin: Real species; a trumpet-shaped single cell up to ~1-2 mm — among the largest single cells — famous since Jennings (1906) for its escalating repertoire of avoidance behaviours. REAL shelf.

attributes: One cell with a macronucleus like a string of beads, cortical rows of cilia, and a contractile body. Jennings described a hierarchy when irritated (e.g. by carmine particles): bend away, reverse cilia, contract, detach and swim off — escalating responses as if choosing among options, in a single cell. It regenerates from fragments (any piece with macronuclear material can rebuild), and recent work revisits its learning with modern rigour.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — the behavioural hierarchy is documented observation (1906, repeatedly confirmed as behaviour); interpreting it as decision-making or learning remains debated, and modern replication-grade learning claims are still being tested. Grade reflects that live status.
brain_profile.architecture: No neurons — the cell cortex is the computer: mechanosensitive channels trigger contraction (myonemes), ciliary reversal is calcium-driven, and response thresholds shift with recent history in ways Jennings read as experience-dependence. Whether that shift is true associative learning or response dynamics is the open question this record preserves.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)

source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

attributes: Its avoiding reaction is membrane biophysics: bump at the front -> calcium influx -> cilia reverse -> the cell backs up, turns, and tries a new heading; touch at the rear does the opposite. This excitable membrane — action-potential-like, ion-channel-based — is a functional ancestor of neuronal excitability. Older claims of paramecium learning (e.g. tube-escape training) have a chequered replication history and are not carried as fact.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — excitability and the avoiding reaction are MEASURED physiology; no learning is claimed. The record's value is the membrane itself: excitability before neurons.
brain_profile.architecture: No neurons, one membrane: voltage-gated calcium channels in the cilia turn touch into reversal. Chemosensory inputs bias turning rates (accumulation in good water, dispersal from bad — klinokinesis-like behaviour). The whole sensorimotor loop is a handful of ion channels — E. coli's logic rebuilt in a eukaryote with electricity.

origin: Real species; a filter-feeding sea squirt whose tadpole larva swims with a chordate body plan — notochord, dorsal nerve cord, and a small cerebral vesicle with an eye and a gravity sensor — then settles, resorbs its tail and much of that larval nervous system, and lives sessile. source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

attributes: The larva is a miniature chordate: ~177 central neurons (published connectome work), a pigment-cup eye (ocellus) and a statocyst-like otolith for orientation. At metamorphosis it digests its own tail and reduces the cerebral vesicle to a small adult ganglion — the famous (and loosely worded) 'eats its own brain' story; precisely: it resorbs most of the larval CNS because a sessile filter-feeder needs far less of it. Adults retain a cerebral ganglion coordinating siphon and feeding responses.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — larval connectomics are published (MEASURED anchor); adult cognition is minimal and unstudied beyond reflexes, and the record says so.
brain_profile.architecture: Two nervous systems in one life: a larval CNS built for a one-day swimming dispersal (find light, gravity, then a surface), and an adult ganglion built for plumbing (siphon control, water flow, gamete release). Metamorphosis is a controlled demolition between the two designs — the Atlas's clearest record that brains are built for a life-stage, not for life.

origin: Real species; a lobate comb jelly of Atlantic American coasts (and a damaging invader in European seas), propelled by eight iridescent comb rows. Ctenophores may have evolved neurons independently of all other animals. REAL shelf.

attributes: A gelatinous predator of zooplankton and fish larvae with a nerve net, an apical sensory organ (statocyst) coordinating the comb rows, and a genome that lacks many canonical bilaterian neurotransmitter pathways — evidence behind the published hypothesis that ctenophore neurons evolved independently (a second invention of the neuron). Chemically it runs a partly different neurotransmitter toolkit (glutamate prominent; several familiar systems absent) — alien wiring solving familiar problems.
